scenes.say: Losing $100 hurts way more than finding $100 feels good. Your brain is not fair with you.
It's called loss aversion. Same amount of money, very different feelings.
Kahneman and Tversky measured it in 1992.
scenes.note: Source: Tversky & Kahneman (1992), Journal of Risk and Uncertainty

scenes.say: A loss weighs about {pain} times as much as an equal gain.
That's why people hold losing positions too long and sell winners too early.
They're not avoiding risk. They're avoiding a feeling.
Before you decide, ask: if losing didn't sting, would I choose differently?

takeaway: Before you decide, ask: if losing didn't sting, would I choose differently?
